attributes.context: This provision is found under the heading “B. REGISTERING FAREBOX” in the current chunk, which also includes an “Effective Date for Section 6A” provision. It sets operator duties and Agency allowances triggered by the purchase of a registering farebox system.

extraction_text: If Bi-State purchases a registering farebox system, operators shall be responsible for monitoring and operating registering farebox equipment and for recording any or all passenger and revenue information relative to the farebox. If an operator's workday is lengthened because of any requirement to turn in or audit his daily work report, the Agency will provide a turn-in allowance for such procedures in accordance with the contract. If an operator's workday is lengthened because of travel to turn in or audit his daily work time, employee shall be compensated at the appropriate contract rate.

attributes.context: This provision is in Section 67 (Break-In Pay), which also provides extra pay for breaking in student operators and Federal minimum wage pay for re-training after accidents or LRV Operating Rule Violations.

extraction_text: An employee who is required to break in as an LRV Operator or become familiar with new procedures or new equipment shall be paid the regular rate of pay during said period for the number of hours required by the Agency.

attributes.context: Appears in Section 10, Break-In Pay, which also provides operators an extra fifty cents per hour or part of an hour for breaking in student operators.

extraction_text: An employee who, for any reason other than his voluntary choice, is required to break in as a bus operator or familiarize himself with a route or new equipment shall be paid his regular rate of pay during said period for the number of hours required by the Agency. If during such period, he is relieved from the performance of his regular work or if the Agency elects that said period be carried on without relieving the employee from his regular work, he shall be paid for such period at the prevailing federal minimum wage for the number of hours required by the Agency.
